requirements.requirement: node3 has a single gateway address to reach node4 across the router pair
requirements.summary: VyOS VRRP groups SEG-A/SEG-B configured on node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100) with a shared VIP (10.50.1.254 / 10.50.2.254) on each private segment. node3's route table shows a single route to 10.50.2.0/24 via 10.50.1.254 dev eth1 (the VIP, not either router's own address), and node4 mirrors this with a single route via 10.50.2.254. Direct ping from node3 to node4 across this route succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Gateway stays available (bounded disruption, no lasting outage) when node1 is down
requirements.summary: node1's eth1/eth2 were taken down to simulate a router outage; node2 transitioned to VRRP MASTER on both segments within ~7 seconds. A background ping running throughout the outage recorded 54/60 packets delivered (10% loss, consistent with the brief VRRP failover gap) with no sustained loss, and a follow-up ping after the transition succeeded cleanly, directly demonstrating a bounded disruption and restored connectivity through node2.

requirements.requirement: Gateway prefers node1 once it is healthy again
requirements.summary: After node1's interfaces were restored, VRRP preemption returned node1 to MASTER on both segments within seconds while node2 fell back to BACKUP, and connectivity from node3 to node4 was reconfirmed healthy, directly demonstrating preference for node1.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes with recovered state
requirements.summary: Each node shows a pre-restart boot id and healthy state, an explicit reboot command, and a distinct post-restart boot id, cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshot (node1 4d3d86e2..., node2 1653235c..., node3 08801285..., node4 1477dae3...). Post-restart, VRRP roles were reconfirmed (node1 MASTER/priority 200, node2 BACKUP/priority 100 on both segments) and static routes/connectivity between node3 and node4 were reverified end to end.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: a single-gateway route on node3 via a shared VRRP VIP that prefers node1 (priority 200) over node2 (priority 100), a demonstrated bounded-disruption failover to node2 when node1's links were taken down, demonstrated preemption back to node1 once restored, and a fully evidenced restart/recovery cycle (changed boot ids, corroborated by the fixed after-executor snapshot, plus reconfirmed VRRP roles and end-to-end connectivity) on all four nodes. Operational hygiene is good: a handful of bounded, low-risk exploratory IP assignments used to empirically determine segment membership were promptly reverted, and only trivial log-file residue was left on node3/node4.
limitations: No independent packet capture or third-party timing measurement of the failover gap exists beyond the executor-run background ping log; the 10% loss figure is self-reported by the executor's own test but is consistent with expected VRRP convergence time.

Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) on node3 and node4 in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package-manager consistency after configuration changes could not be independently verified.
The evaluator cannot verify from static config alone whether the VRRP setup would survive a config-sync/persistence check beyond the one reboot cycle observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor made several bounded, temporary IP-address mutations on all four nodes (cmd-cc8fb3199c864e9d, cmd-bc166a07584e4d02, cmd-980f1a54d2ce4107, cmd-971c7919398849ab) purely to empirically confirm which physical segment each interface belonged to before committing the real VyOS/RHEL configuration; all of these were explicitly reverted moments later (cmd-48d4fffcd27c456e, cmd-dd965e16b2f54cb9, cmd-286d2c1e31c442ce, cmd-6bc0f0b7fb0948d7) and left no residue in the final lifecycle snapshot. These were low-risk, low-blast-radius discovery steps that informed the correct VRRP group placement (a legitimate prerequisite) rather than an unrelated experiment, so they are treated leniently. Minor residue was left behind: /tmp/failover_ping.log, /tmp/failover_ping.pid, and /tmp/reboot.log on node3, and /tmp/reboot.log on node4, visible in the after-executor snapshot temporary-files diff — small, non-sensitive leftover files from the executor's own testing that were not cleaned up. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no weakened security controls were observed in either node's before/after comparison.
